rules.title: Off-road diesel rule covers vehicles of 25 hp or more
rules.plain_english: CARB's off-road diesel fleet rule applies to anyone who owns or operates in California a self-propelled off-road diesel vehicle (excavator, loader, dozer, backhoe, crane, forklift and the like) with an engine of 25 horsepower or more, including rented and leased machines. Two-engine cranes, drill rigs and similar vehicles with a 50 bhp or larger auxiliary engine are also covered.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source_location: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 3, §2449(b)(1)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 3)
rules.verbatim_quote: Except as provided in subsection (b)(2) below, this regulation applies to any person, business, or government agency who owns or operates within California any vehicles with a diesel-fueled or alternative diesel fueled off-road compression-ignition engine with maximum power (max hp) of 25 horsepower (hp) or greater provided that the vehicle cannot be registered and driven safely on-road or was not designed to be driven on-road, even if it has been modified so that it can be driven safely on-road.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. Exempt: vehicles used solely for agriculture, personal-use vehicles, vehicles awaiting sale (2449(e)(10)-(11)); emergency-only, snow-removal and over-half-agricultural vehicles still report and label.

rules.title: Off-road fleet size: small up to 2,500 hp, medium 2,501-5,000 hp, large over 5,000 hp
rules.plain_english: Fleet size is set by adding the horsepower of every off-road diesel vehicle under common ownership or control. Over 5,000 hp is a large fleet, 2,500 hp or less is a small fleet, and anything in between is medium. All state and federal government fleets count as large, whatever their size.

rules.plain_english: A machine rented or leased for less than one year belongs to the rental company's fleet for CARB purposes. A lease of one year or more can move the machine into the renter's fleet, but only if the written lease says so.

rules.title: Off-road diesel equipment may not idle more than 5 minutes
rules.plain_english: No off-road diesel machine may idle for more than five minutes in a row. Exceptions: waiting in a work queue, safety checks, servicing, idling needed to do the machine's work (such as running a crane), warming up to operating temperature, and idling needed for safe operation. For a rented machine, the renter is responsible, and the rental agreement must say so.

exceptions: work the vehicle was designed for (e.g., crane)
parameters.waiver: Executive Officer may grant a written waiver on justification

Idling of a vehicle that is owned by a rental company is the responsibility of the renter or lessee, and the rental agreement shall so indicate. The idling limit does not apply to: 1. idling when queuing, 2. idling to verify that the vehicle is in safe operating condition, 3. idling for testing, servicing, repairing or diagnostic purposes, 4. idling necessary to accomplish work for which the vehicle was designed (such as operating a crane), 5. idling required to bring the machine system to operating temperature, and 6. idling necessary to ensure safe operation of the vehicle.

rules.title: Permanent low-use vehicle: under 200 hours a year

rules.plain_english: For true emergency projects, primes and public agencies do not need the fleet certificates, but must keep records showing the equipment was used only for the emergency: a description, the location, the dates, and the fleet's attestation. rules.title: Truck and Bus rule covers diesel vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR
rules.plain_english: CARB's Truck and Bus regulation applies to diesel (and dual-fuel or alternative diesel) trucks and buses with a manufacturer's gross vehicle weight rating over 14,000 pounds that run in California, whether owned, leased or rented, and to people selling them. Not covered (2025(c)): emergency and military tactical vehicles, off-road vehicles, dedicated snow-removal vehicles, historic vehicles, motor homes for non-commercial private use, personal-use pickups of 19,500 lb or less, solid waste collection and public transit vehicles under their own rules, municipal vehicles that meet the public agency fleet rule (13 CCR 2022.1) BACT requirements, and two-engine cranes, drill rigs and workover rigs that are under the off-road rule.

A passing test may be submitted no more than 90 days before a compliance deadline; for example, a vehicle with a January 1, 2025 deadline could submit a test from October 1, 2024.

rules.title: Clean Truck Check deadlines follow the DMV registration date
rules.plain_english: For California-registered trucks the compliance year runs from the DMV registration expiration date. Twice-a-year deadlines fall on that day in months 6 and 12; quarterly deadlines in months 3, 6, 9 and 12. For vehicles registered outside California or exempt from DMV registration, the compliance year starts and ends on the last day of a month set by the last digit of the VIN: 0 October, 1 November, 2 December, 3 January, 4 February, 5 March, 6 April, 7 May, 8 June, 9 July.

rules.title: Clean Truck Check annual compliance fee: $30 base, adjusted yearly for inflation
rules.plain_english: Each registered heavy-duty vehicle owes CARB an annual compliance fee before its first compliance for the year. The regulation set it at $30.00 and CARB adjusts it each year by the California Consumer Price Index, publishing the new amount by July 1.

rules.title: Bay Area: check each exit for track-out twice a workday and keep logs 2 years
rules.plain_english: Large sites that produce track-out must check each active exit at least twice every workday at peak exit times, log which exits were checked, log every time track-out exceeded 25 feet and the cleanup done, and keep the records two years for the District.

verification_meta.method: Independent re-verification of all 138 rules, every category, on 2026-11-25. Each source_location URL was fetched fresh with curl into a new directory and its text extracted with pdftotext (layout and reading order) and pdfplumber. The builder's text files and quote checker were not used. For CARB's strike/underline documents (the 15-Day Modified Text and the Final Regulation Order), struck-out characters were removed by a new strike-line detector: horizontal rules crossing 35-75% of glyph height. Only the strike-removed text was accepted for quotes. Every verbatim_quote, and each ' [...] '-separated passage, was string-matched after normalizing whitespace, quote marks and dashes. Every parameter value, threshold, date, citation and applies_to scope was read against the text. CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (froa-1.pdf, Attachment A-1, created Aug. 17, 2023) downloaded normally (HTTP 200). A word-level diff against the 15-day text showed about 270 differences, almost all punctuation, digits vs. words, or capitalization. One substantive deletion affected this pack: the 'penalty of perjury' sentence in 2449(g). Off-Road rules now cite the Final Regulation Order first. The Final Regulation Order, the Clean Truck Check Periodic Testing Requirements fact sheet (Mar. 13, 2024) and the DMV-registration FAQ (2020) were located by web search restricted to arb.ca.gov and downloaded from ww2.arb.ca.gov. The last two resolved the two rules that had been read_from_primary_text=false. The Off-Road booklet cited in the notes was also fetched and read. BAAQMD's About page was read for the nine-county scope. CARB HTML pages (Clean Truck Check overview and fee-update pages) and the 2019 SB 1 fact sheet PDF returned CARB's HTTP 419 rate-limit page, which was not bypassed. atrn.assembly.ca.gov is outside the allowed hosts, and leginfo.legislature.ca.gov was not used, so Health and Safety Code / Vehicle Code text (penalty dollar amounts; VC 4000.15) remains unread and is labelled as such. Statuses: confirmed = quote and all parameters match the official text; corrected = a parameter, quote, citation, source_location, effective date or the meaning of title/plain_english was changed against the text (the correction field says what changed); unverifiable = primary text could not be read (none remain); refuted = contradicted or absent and removed (none). Note-only fixes are listed in non_parameter_edits and keep status confirmed. Adversarial review 2026-11-25 re-fetched all 24 source PDFs (HTTP 200, identical sha256 prefixes), re-extracted them independently and corrected 17 rules: air-ctc-deadline-alignment, air-ctc-testing-frequency, air-ord-annual-reporting-march-1, air-ord-enforcement-status-2025, air-perp-fleet-size-750, air-perp-portable-12-months, air-perp-portable-atcm-50bhp, air-scaqmd403-large-operation, air-scaqmd4031-coachella-dust-plan, air-sjv8021-exemptions, air-sjv8021-small-site-48-hour-notice, air-sjv8041-trackout-device-triggers, air-tb-2010-engine-required, air-tb-applicability-14000, air-tb-nox-exempt-areas, air-truck-idling-5-minutes, air-truck-idling-fine-1000-day. Each correction names the passage added.
